name: Yvette Weber
life: “I still remember waiting beside a door that echoed like my old tenement.” On Wednesday, near the entrance to the Wash House, Yvette stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I want the new worker to knock twice. A single knock still sounds like a debt collector at my old front door.
appearance: Yvette has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose. Look for short white hair and darker eyebrows. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. In conversation Yvette rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Yvette can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To have the new worker knock twice.
family: Ellen Scott is Yvette’s cousin. Yvette is free to hang up first. Ellen makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The painted footprint*, Ellen says, “I ran barefoot races here. I want to know whether the old starting mark lies under that plank.”
connections: Harry Rhodes. A private introduction lets a client ask both for a particular knock and for medicine on a reachable shelf.

reactions.situation: The successor asks for a private introduction at the door
reactions.response: Yvette introduces the successor quietly and gives the client a chance to set the routine.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Yvette calls for emergency assistance from outside and waits to give the street number.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Yvette asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
